A missing port, missing or unreadable record, or any `verify_cold_inputs` mismatch becomes `LabControlRefused("FROZEN_RUN_NOT_RECONSTRUCTIBLE", run.run_id, detail)` before Stage, schedule or gateway admission. No current-head or fixture fallback.
+
+For a cold run, `start` verifies frozen inputs and executes the whole inclusive minute-boundary interval `[19:00,20:00]` once: 61 boundaries, 60 minutes. Return a terminal `LabProjection`: `status=COMPLETED`, `boundaries_completed=boundaries_total=61`, `offset_minutes=60`, `simulation_time=interval_end_time=2026-10-06T20:00:00Z`, `interval_start_time=2026-10-06T19:00:00Z`, `timestep_minutes=1`, frozen seed and profile IDs/versions, existing kernel/numeric/contract constants, `inputs_identity=run_identity_sha256(run)`, `content_digest=SHA-256(canonical_json(["cold-thermal/1", ordered exact private minute-record documents]))`, and `observation_series_digest=SHA-256(canonical_json(ordered DeviceReport V2 texts))` including held reports before release. Define the exact minute-record renderer in one cold adapter function and use it for the digest and private artifact; never derive it from product evidence. `private_state`, `observations`, `signals`, `reporting_gaps`, `recent_reports` are empty tuples; `reported_count` is all generated reports including held, `suppressed_by_gap_count=dropped_count=0`, `failure=electrical=None`. Notes state that the cold details live in the private artifact and gateway Stage, so empty legacy views make no claim about the physical trajectory. The Draft projection has the same frozen identities/timing, `NOT_STARTED`, zero completed boundaries, empty-series digest, no content digest and empty views; it must bypass legacy `_reporting_for`/`_model_for`. After cold `start`, `step` and `run_to_end` refuse `ALREADY_TERMINAL`; before it, both refuse `NOT_STARTED`.
+
+Persist through `JsonExecutionArtifacts` with a distinct schema marker `artifact_schema_version: 6`, `execution_kind: COLD`, `run_identity_sha256`, scenario and observation SHA, the complete-window projection fields/digests and report count. `render_projection`/`parse_projection` must round-trip and strictly validate these; old schemas 1-5 keep their bytes, and damaged/future cold artifacts read `ARTIFACT_UNREADABLE`. Keep minute records/history in that private artifact only; a cold history read uses an explicit cold private document or an honest `HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE` result, never the legacy electrical history. `_execution_status` must read `COMPLETED` from the artifact after restart before `release_registered`; a live handle alone is insufficient. Write the terminal artifact after successful ordinary Stage admission through the closing ordinary instant; any refusal leaves the run unreleasable and records the refusal.
+

Each held report becomes `DelayedReport` with its unchanged report text/source time and `scheduled_release_at=2026-10-06T20:10:00Z`; use a stable `delay_event_id` derived from its report key. Set schedule `world_reached_instant=2026-10-06T20:00:03Z`, `world_complete=True`, `world_boundaries_completed=61`; pass ordinary instants to existing `_release`. The held 19:20 report remains pending until `advance_publication(run,"2026-10-06T20:10:00Z")`; gateway stamps that release as `published_at`, retains 19:20 `source_time`, and deduplicates retries by report key. A missing durable schedule after execution refuses, rather than rebuilding from the world.

For each disposition, parse the canonical `ingestion_batch.batch_text` Batch V2 and take the envelope at its ordinal, SHA-256 its canonical UTF-8 text, then append the JSON array `[external_batch_id,ordinal,envelope_sha256,decision,accepted_evidence_id_or_null]` to the ordered digest input. `public_digest=SHA-256(UTF8(canonical_json(that array)))`. A rejected/conflict row uses null for this final element; a duplicate uses its referenced accepted ID. Refuse missing ordinals, invalid canonical batch text, mismatched batch commitment or scope as 503. This digest commits to public envelopes and dispositions only; no private trajectory, forcing, report payload or run truth appears in the API.

## Commit (4) exact contract

**Replay storage and API.** Add read-only `ColdReplayService` in `backend/assetops_backend/cold_replay.py`, backed by an injected read-only Postgres adapter and `SimulationRunRepository`; no SQL belongs in the API or a new writer. `build_cold_replay_router` mounts `GET /api/sites/{site_code}/cold/replay?run_id=<id>` only under the Lab gate. Require exactly one nonempty `run_id`; missing/extra/unknown query keys answer 422 `COLD_REPLAY_PARAMETER_INVALID`. Use the existing `Access(request,site_code)` seam and an owner-role check supplied by production composition: 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, 403 `SITE_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN` for foreign tenant or role, 404 `SITE_NOT_FOUND`/`RUN_NOT_FOUND` for an admitted caller's unknown Site/run. A selected run must belong to the authenticated tenant and Site, have the cold model/publication/observation pair and a registered basis; never read a different run's lineage. The development access function is for injected tests only; no production owner principal means 403, not an implicit operator grant. A registered publication for the run with another source class is excluded, and an inaccessible source gate returns 403. Run-store/ledger read failure, corrupt run or a missing persisted run referenced by a publication returns 503 `COLD_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE`; do not infer profile data from publications. A valid persisted cold run with no publications returns 200 with `publication_id:null`, empty arrays and SHA-256 of canonical `[]`.

The response has exactly `publication_id` (latest UUID string or null), `publication_ids` (UUID strings), `run_profile:{model_profile:{profile_id,profile_version},publication_profile:{profile_id,profile_version},observation_profile:{profile_id,profile_version}}`, `scenario_digest` (frozen SHA), `batch_ids` (external Batch V2 IDs), `receipts` (one `{batch_id,accepted,duplicate,rejected,conflict}` per linked batch), `accepted_record_ids` (UUID strings for `ACCEPTED` dispositions only), and `public_digest`. Order publications by `(evidence_publication.recorded_at,evidence_publication.id)` and linked batches by that order; a publication without a linked batch is a typed 503 because its receipt cannot be claimed. Use `batch_publication_link` on all scoped IDs and `ingestion_batch`, then `ingestion_disposition` by `(batch_id,ordinal)`; recompute all four counts from dispositions, never `ingestion_batch` cached totals. `accepted_record_ids` includes the first accepted ID at its accepted ordinal and excludes duplicate references; `CONFLICT` is counted separately from `REJECTED`. For each disposition, parse the canonical `ingestion_batch.batch_text` Batch V2 and take the envelope at its ordinal, SHA-256 its canonical UTF-8 text, then append the JSON array `[external_batch_id,ordinal,envelope_sha256,decision,accepted_evidence_id_or_null]` to the ordered digest input. `public_digest=SHA-256(UTF8(canonical_json(that array)))`. A rejected/conflict row uses null for this final element; a duplicate uses its referenced accepted ID. Refuse missing ordinals, invalid canonical batch text, mismatched batch commitment or scope as 503. This digest commits to public envelopes and dispositions only; no private trajectory, forcing, report payload or run truth appears in the API.

**Six manifest files.** `contract-fixtures/w2/cold/{normal,excursion,backup-failed,missing-probe,late-reading,contradictory}.json` use canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, final newline) and exactly the keys named in the test paragraph above. `model_profile`, `publication_profile`, `observation_profile` are `{profile_id,profile_version}`; `window` is `{start:"2026-10-06T19:00:00Z",end:"2026-10-06T20:05:00Z",end_exclusive:true}`; `envelope_sha256` is the ordered array of canonical envelope digests, `batch_sha256` the ordered array of canonical Batch V2 payload digests, `receipt_dispositions` the ordered array of `{batch_id,ordinal,decision,accepted_evidence_id}` and `accepted_evidence_ids` the ordered accepted-only ID array. `assertions` is a closed object with `chamber_point_count`, `event_kinds` (ordered public kinds), `unavailable_count`, `late_source_time`, `late_published_at`, `start_result_at`, `transfer_result_at`, `high_1915`, `high_1920`; inapplicable fields are null. `schema="cold-replay-manifest/1"`, `site_code="COLD-LAB-001"`, `seed=20417`, and the six scenario IDs/digests and frozen revision IDs come from the registered fixture. `late-reading` has 12 chamber points before 20:10 release and 13 after; its manifest captures the completed post-release replay, while the test asserts both phases. All other cases have 13 except `missing-probe` with 7. A manifest is generated once from a fully executed registered path, reviewed, then pinned; the test never rewrites it during assertion.

**Determinism and six Postgres proofs.** `backend/tests/test_w202_cold_replay_postgres.py` uses only `assetops_w202c_test` or another private `*_test` DB. Order publications by `(evidence_publication.recorded_at,evidence_publication.id)` and linked batches by that order; an unlinked publication is a valid pending release and contributes its ID but no batch/receipt/accepted IDs; a linked batch that is `IN_PROGRESS` or has incomplete dispositions is a 503 `COLD_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE`, never a partial completed receipt. A rejected/conflict row uses null for this final element; a duplicate uses its referenced accepted ID. This digest commits to public envelopes and dispositions only; no private trajectory, forcing, report payload or run truth appears in the API.

A valid persisted cold run with no publications returns 200 with `publication_id:null`, empty arrays and SHA-256 of canonical `[]`.

+The response has exactly `publication_id` (latest UUID string or null), `publication_ids` (UUID strings), `run_profile:{model_profile:{profile_id,profile_version},publication_profile:{profile_id,profile_version},observation_profile:{profile_id,profile_version}}`, `scenario_digest` (frozen SHA), `batch_ids` (external Batch V2 IDs), `receipts` (one `{batch_id,accepted,duplicate,rejected,conflict}` per linked batch), `accepted_record_ids` (UUID strings for `ACCEPTED` dispositions only), and `public_digest`. Order publications by `(evidence_publication.recorded_at,evidence_publication.id)` and linked batches by that order; an unlinked publication is a valid pending release and contributes its ID but no batch/receipt/accepted IDs; a linked batch that is `IN_PROGRESS` or has incomplete dispositions is a 503 `COLD_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE`, never a partial completed receipt. A rejected/conflict row uses null for this final element; a duplicate uses its referenced accepted ID. Refuse missing ordinals, invalid canonical batch text, mismatched batch commitment or scope as 503. This digest commits to public envelopes and dispositions only; no private trajectory, forcing, report payload or run truth appears in the API.

+The response has exactly `publication_id` (latest UUID string or null), `publication_ids` (UUID strings), `run_profile:{model_profile:{profile_id,profile_version},publication_profile:{profile_id,profile_version},observation_profile:{profile_id,profile_version}}`, `scenario_digest` (frozen SHA), `batch_ids` (external Batch V2 IDs), `receipts` (one `{batch_id,accepted,duplicate,rejected,conflict}` per linked batch), `accepted_record_ids` (UUID strings for `ACCEPTED` dispositions only), and `public_digest`. Order publications by `(evidence_publication.recorded_at,evidence_publication.id)` and linked batches by that order; an unlinked publication is a valid pending release and contributes its ID but no batch/receipt/accepted IDs; a linked batch that is `IN_PROGRESS` or has incomplete dispositions is a 503 `COLD_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE`, never a partial completed receipt. Use `batch_publication_link` on all scoped IDs and `ingestion_batch`, then `ingestion_disposition` by `(batch_id,ordinal)`; recompute all four counts from dispositions, never `ingestion_batch` cached totals. `accepted_record_ids` includes the first accepted ID at its accepted ordinal and excludes duplicate references; `CONFLICT` is counted separately from `REJECTED`. For each disposition, parse the canonical `ingestion_batch.batch_text` Batch V2 and take the envelope at its ordinal, SHA-256 its canonical UTF-8 text, then append the JSON array `[external_batch_id,ordinal,envelope_sha256,decision,accepted_evidence_id_or_null]` to the ordered digest input. `public_digest=SHA-256(UTF8(canonical_json(that array)))`. A rejected/conflict row uses null for this final element; a duplicate uses its referenced accepted ID. Refuse missing ordinals, invalid canonical batch text, mismatched batch commitment or scope as 503. This digest commits to public envelopes and dispositions only; no private trajectory, forcing, report payload or run truth appears in the API.
